# viettelcloud_server (Resource)

Manage a Viettel Cloud server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "viettelcloud_vpc" "example" {
  name   = "server-example-vpc"
  cidr   = "10.0.0.0/16"
  region = { name = "vn-central-1" }
}

resource "viettelcloud_subnet" "example" {
  name = "server-example-subnet"
  cidr = "10.0.1.0/24"
  vpc  = { id = viettelcloud_vpc.example.id }
}

resource "viettelcloud_volume" "existing" {
  name = "independent-server-volume"
  size = 20
  zone = { name = "vn-central-1a" }
  create_from = {
    source_type = "empty"
    volume_type = { name = "Ceph_HDD_1A_10K" }
  }
}

resource "viettelcloud_server" "example" {
  name = "example-server"
  zone = { name = "vn-central-1a" }

  flavor = {
    kind   = "custom"
    family = "basic"
    vcpus  = 2
    ram    = 2
  }

  boot = {
    boot_type   = "image"
    image       = { os = "Ubuntu", version = "22.04" }
    volume_type = { disk_type = "ssd", speed = "10k", multiattach = false }
    volume_size = 30
  }

  private_ips = [{
    kind   = "subnet"
    subnet = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }
  }]

  data_volumes = [
    {
      kind        = "new"
      volume_type = { name = "Ceph_HDD_1A_10K" }
      volume_size = 20
    },
    {
      kind = "existing"
      id   = viettelcloud_volume.existing.id
    },
  ]
}
```

## Data Volume Identity

The provider uses each volume ID to identify an attachment.
For `kind = "new"`, omit `id` when you create the server.
State records the resources that Terraform manages.
After creation, state contains the allocated ID.
For later updates, you can set `id` to that value to identify the volume.
An unchanged list keeps its existing IDs, even when volumes share the same type and size.

If several prior volumes match a changed entry, the provider stops with an error before it changes any volume.
Set each retained entry's `id` to its intended ID from state.
Then apply the change again.
This also applies when you remove one volume and resize another in one apply.

## Schema

### Required

- `boot` (Attributes) Boot configuration. Supported boot types are image, custom_image, local_disk, and volume. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--boot))
- `flavor` (Attributes) Predefined or custom server flavor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flavor))
- `name` (String) Server name.

### Optional

- `bandwidth` (Number) Server bandwidth in Mbps. The backend enforces the supported range and rejects a value below its minimum, so omit it to accept the backend default.
- `data_volumes` (Attributes List) Data volume attachments. kind new creates a volume, and kind existing attaches a volume by ID. Omission preserves attachments. An empty list detaches all data volumes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data_volumes))
- `description` (String) Optional server description. Omitting it preserves the backend value; set an empty string to clear it.
- `elastic_ips` (Attributes List) Elastic IP attachments. kind existing attaches an IP; kind new creates an IP. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--elastic_ips))
- `key_pair` (Attributes) Key pair associated with the server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--key_pair))
- `placement_group` (Attributes) Placement group associated with the server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--placement_group))
- `power_state` (String) Desired power state. Supported values are running and shutdown.
- `private_ips` (Attributes List) Private IP attachments. kind subnet creates an IP; kind ip attaches an existing IP. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--private_ips))
- `quantity` (Number) Number of servers to create. A Terraform server resource manages exactly one server, so only 1 is supported.
- `security_groups` (Attributes Set) Security groups attached to the server. Configure an empty set to detach all security groups. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--security_groups))
- `user_data` (String, Sensitive) Cloud-init user data.
- `zone` (Attributes) Project zone that hosts the server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--zone))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC3339).
- `data_volume_ids` (List of String) Attached data volume IDs.
- `id` (String) Server ID (UUID).
- `key_pair_name` (String) Key pair name associated with the server.
- `placement_group_name` (String) Placement group name associated with the server.
- `server_type` (String) Backend server type.
- `status` (String) Current lifecycle status.

Changed criteria keep the current type when it still matches. Required for kind new. Selecting a different type updates the volume in place. The backend supplies the type for kind existing. ## Import

Import the server by its UUID.
The API does not identify which owner created each attached data volume.
The provider imports data volumes as `kind = "existing"` with `delete_on_termination = false`.
If you omit `data_volumes`, the provider preserves those attachments and their cleanup flags.

If you keep `data_volumes` in configuration, set each entry to `kind = "existing"` with its attached volume ID.
Replace the earlier entries that contain only `volume_type` and `volume_size`.
Those entries default to `kind = "new"`.
If you keep them after import, the provider creates new volumes and detaches the imported volumes.
Omit `volume_type`, `volume_size`, and `iops` for existing entries because the backend supplies those values.

If the server must delete an imported data volume on destroy, explicitly set that entry's `delete_on_termination = true`.
The default preserves imported data volumes after server destruction.
Use the server ID, attachment IDs, and server attributes from the imported state in this example.

```terraform
import {
  to = viettelcloud_server.imported
  id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
}

resource "viettelcloud_server" "imported" {
  name   = "existing-server"
  zone   = { name = "vn-central-1a" }
  flavor = { kind = "predefined", name = "b1.micro2x" }
  boot = {
    boot_type   = "image"
    image       = { name = "ubuntu-22.04-publiccloud" }
    volume_type = { name = "Ceph_HDD_1A_10K" }
    volume_size = 30
  }

  data_volumes = [{
    kind                  = "existing"
    id                    = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
    delete_on_termination = false
  }]
}
```
